$comment: D-CSUBSET-VLA-WIN64-UNWIND: the end-to-end STACK-WALK witness. `vla_frame` holds a VLA OBJECT and MAKES CALLS (the D-CSUBSET-VLA-NONLEAF-CALL-FRAME shape) and sits as a MIDDLE frame in main --__try--> level1 --> vla_frame --> trap, so a hardware access violation makes the OS unwind THROUGH the runtime-moved frame twice — once virtually while searching for a handler, and once for real through RtlUnwindEx to build the context the __except body resumes on. A build proves bytes were emitted; this proves the OS reads them and lands in the right place. ✔MEASURED, and it REFUTES this row's stated premise: the pe64 UNWIND_INFO for a VLA function ALREADY carries UWOP_SET_FPREG (`01 4a 13 05` / `4a 03` / …, FrameRegister rbp, FrameOffset 0) at the frame-pointer capture, because lir_callconv records a `def_cfa_register` CFI op there and link/format/pe.cpp translates that to SET_FPREG. And the row's other half does not exist: Win64 has NO dynamic-alloca unwind opcode — the frame register IS the mechanism, which is exactly what the pe64 ORACLE does (mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 emits SET_FPREG plus the fixed prologue's codes and NOTHING for its `sub %rax,%rsp`). ⚠ THIS EXAMPLE IS AN END-TO-END PROOF, NOT A RED-ON-DISABLE DISCRIMINATOR FOR SET_FPREG, and that is ✔MEASURED rather than assumed: with the SET_FPREG emission suppressed in pe.cpp this program STILL exits 42, because the Windows dispatcher, handed a wrong RSP, falls back to a leaf-style pop and marches up the stack 8 bytes at a time until it stumbles on the real return address. So 'the process survived an exception' is a weaker instrument than it looks. The DISCRIMINATING pins for the same property live elsewhere and both go red under that mutation: `tests/link/test_pe_writer.cpp` VlaFramePointerCaptureEmitsSetFpregSoTheFrameIsDescribable asserts the three bytes (CountOfCodes, FrameRegister, the code pair), and a direct RtlCaptureContext/RtlVirtualUnwind drive over the same frame returns Rip 0 instead of landing in level1 (that one cannot be a corpus example: it needs `--resolve-library` against an absolute system DLL, which the manifest vocabulary deliberately refuses). What THIS example still catches on its own is the frame model underneath it — with the outgoing-args watermark bias removed it exits 11, because `vla_frame` never reaches its trap. pe64-ONLY: x64 SEH + __C_specific_handler + windows.h are Windows. No reference toolchain compiles this exact source — mingw-w64 gcc rejects `__try` and MSVC rejects the VLA (`error C2057`), each probed separately; both features are shipped DSS behaviour witnessed by their own examples. No optimizedPipelines arm, as with the sibling `seh_catch_*` examples.
